problem_type: PR board-claim parser rejects real board filenames containing digits
symptom: PR #1322 wrote a valid `## 拍板图` claim for a board with a digit, but merge-preflight reported that the UI change had no board claim because the claim line was discarded.
direct_cause: scripts/check-board-parity.mjs:CLAIM_LINE used `([A-Za-z]+)` for the board token, so `IconsF1`, `ComposerB3`, and `Director3dbox` never reached checkPrBoardClaims.
class_root: The shared claim-line parser did not encode the board-name invariant used by docs/design/boards filenames: an ASCII letter first, followed by ASCII letters or digits. Every consumer therefore inherited the same silent omission for any future digit-bearing board.
affected_population: Any PR body claiming a real board whose filename contains one or more digits
Both check-board-parity and the PR-body / merge-preflight judgement path, which share parsePrBoardClaims
entry_points: scripts/check-board-parity.mjs parsePrBoardClaims: parses `## 拍板图` claim lines for board parity
scripts/pr-body-criteria.mjs checkBoardClaim: invokes the same parser for PR judgement and merge-preflight
scripts/pr-body-criteria.mjs checkPrBoardClaims: validates parsed claims against head manifests
internal_only_reason: The invariant is repository-local: board names are the stems of docs/design/boards/*.board.json files and both consumers are in this repository. No third-party runtime decides this syntax.
invariants: Every board claim line accepted by parsePrBoardClaims has a board token matching /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$/.
Every current docs/design/boards/**/*.board.json stem is accepted by the same parser.
A syntactically valid but nonexistent board name still reaches checkPrBoardClaims and fails closed with a board-not-found error.
Board names containing illegal punctuation are not parsed as claims.

door_reduction.why_not: The door map was run with `node scripts/door-map.mjs --read=CLAIM_LINE,parsePrBoardClaims,checkPrBoardClaims,checkBoardClaim --roots=scripts`. The five readers are distinct responsibilities that must remain: CLAIM_LINE and parsePrBoardClaims own syntax extraction; checkPrBoardClaims owns manifest validation; checkBoardClaim is the PR-judgement adapter; pr-body-criteria also calls the shared parser directly for its own empty-claim path. They now all converge on the one parser boundary, so none can be deleted without deleting a judgement surface.

generality_proof: The only production parser for a `## 拍板图` claim line is parsePrBoardClaims, and both board-parity and PR-body judgement call it. The corrected token rule accepts every current board stem, including all digit-bearing stems, while the census test will fail if a future board filename introduces a character outside the declared grammar. Validation remains separate and still rejects nonexistent boards, so broadening syntax cannot turn an unknown board into a pass.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Single syntax boundary for all PR board-claim consumers; recognizes the repository board-name grammar and returns structured claims.
Shared semantic boundary that checks parsed claims against manifests and fails closed for missing or non-implemented elements.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The parser now accepts IconsF1, ComposerB3, Director3dbox and every board stem discovered under docs/design/boards; illegal punctuation remains skipped.
PR judgement imports parsePrBoardClaims and checkPrBoardClaims from check-board-parity.mjs, so merge-preflight and CI use the corrected shared boundary.
The semantic validator still receives parsed digit-bearing claims and reports nonexistent names or invalid element status instead of silently losing the line.

recurrence.reason: Any future board filename or PR body that adds a digit to an otherwise valid board name would reproduce the same silent omission, and every existing consumer shares this parser.
same_class_scan: scripts/check-board-parity.node-test.mjs now checks digit-bearing examples, illegal punctuation, nonexistent names, and a recursive docs/design/boards filename census
scripts/pr-body-criteria.mjs imports parsePrBoardClaims and checkPrBoardClaims; scripts/merge-preflight.mjs reaches that path through evaluatePrBody

prevention.invariant: parsePrBoardClaims is the sole board-claim syntax parser and accepts exactly an ASCII letter followed by ASCII letters or digits for the board token.
prevention.failure_mode: Illegal board-name syntax is skipped; syntactically valid but unknown names are passed to checkPrBoardClaims and produce an explicit board-not-found error.
prevention.strategy: Keep syntax in one shared parser and pin the repository-wide filename population with a census test, so a new board-name shape cannot silently fall outside the parser.

legacy_paths.rationale: No obsolete parser or fallback exists. The existing parser is tightened in place and all consumers continue to import it.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The failure is in repository-local regular-expression parsing; no third-party dependency controls the invariant.

migration: No persisted data migration is needed. Existing alphabetic claims keep their behavior; digit-bearing claims begin parsing; unknown names and punctuation continue to fail or be ignored under the existing contract.
residual_risks: The grammar intentionally remains ASCII letter/digit because that is the character set of every current board stem; a future punctuation or non-ASCII board name will make the census test red and require an explicit syntax decision.
The requested merge-preflight run depends on live PR #1322 availability and gh authentication; local parser and class tests are independent of that network boundary.
